name: Hindsight (Vectorize)
one_line: Postgres/pgvector agent-memory server with three operations (retain = per-chunk LLM fact extraction into world/experience facts plus an entity/temporal/semantic/causal link graph; recall = four parallel retrieval arms fused by RRF, cross-encoder reranked and packed to a token budget with no LLM call; reflect = a tool-using agent over mental models, observations and raw facts), with background LLM consolidation of facts into evidence-backed observations.

locomo.protocol: Vendor leaderboard 'LoComo10'. Our notes: Gemini 3.1 Pro preview reader, Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite judge told to 'be generous', about 36k context. Only the 92% figure was re-confirmed on the site this pass; reader, judge and context are not shown there.

Paper Table 4: Gemini-3 Pro answer generator only; GPT-OSS-120b judge at temperature 0; categories single-hop / multi-hop / open-domain / temporal (86.17 / 70.83 / 95.12 / 83.80); recall token budget left as an unfilled '<add> tokens' placeholder in the paper

arch.product.t: Self-hostable FastAPI server plus worker (Docker, pip, Helm, embedded 'hindsight-all' with a bundled pg0 Postgres), managed Hindsight Cloud, SDKs (Python, TS, Go, CLI), an MCP server and 25+ LLM providers. Packaging: hindsight-api-slim has no local ML stack; hindsight-api = slim[all] adds the local-ml extra (torch, sentence-transformers, flashrank, MLX); hindsight-all(-slim) bundles the server for in-process use.
arch.product.e: README.md (Quick Start); hindsight-api/pyproject.toml:13; hindsight-api-slim/pyproject.toml:109-139; hindsight-all-slim/pyproject.toml; config.py:1100 DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL='pg0' [read]

arch.truth.t: Postgres is the single source of truth: documents (original text kept by default), chunks, memory_units (facts and observations share one table, distinguished by fact_type), entities, links, mental models. Raw source text is kept so documents can be re-extracted.

arch.stores.t: One relational store: PostgreSQL + pgvector (HNSW) for vectors, Postgres full-text for keywords; Oracle AI Database is supported as an alternative. A memories-store abstraction lets a store own its index (recall_unified).
arch.stores.e: README.md (Docker external PostgreSQL, Oracle note); engine/search/retrieval.py:124-131; engine/db/oracle.py [read]; docs/developer/performance.md (HNSW) [doc]

arch.graphdb.t: No graph database. The graph lives in Postgres tables (entities, unit-entity joins, memory_links with link types entity/temporal/semantic/caused_by, entity_cooccurrences), walked with SQL ('link_expansion' retriever).

arch.scope.t: Bank = isolated store per user/agent/project (strict, no cross-bank reads). Inside a bank, tags give visibility scoping on recall/reflect (any/all/exact match, tag groups) and observation_scopes partition consolidation. Multi-tenancy by Postgres schema via a TenantExtension.
arch.scope.e: README.md (Memory Banks); api/http.py:541-560 RecallRequest tags; extensions/tenant.py:54-70 [read]

write.entry.t: POST /v1/default/banks/{bank_id}/memories with items (content, context, timestamp, tags, metadata, document_id); also file retain, MCP retain tool and SDK client.retain. Internally MemoryEngine.retain_batch_async -> retain.orchestrator.retain_batch.

write.receipt.t: Synchronous by default: the call waits until extraction, embedding and storage are committed ('async' defaults to false). With async=true the request is queued in a Postgres async_operations table and claimed by workers with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; large batches are auto-split into sub-batches of ~10,000 tokens. Consolidation always runs later in the background.

write.roles.t: Every fact is classified world vs experience (the schema calls the latter 'assistant') by who is speaking, not grammar. The extractor is told the narrator is the bank's agent unless the caller's context names another first-person speaker, in which case those statements become world facts about that speaker.

write.firewall.t: Memory Defense is opt-in per bank and off by default. The open-source build implements only a 'sensitive_data' rule: 45 regex patterns (API keys, cloud tokens, DB strings, Luhn-checked cards, PII) with redact or block actions, webhook and audit entries. No prompt-injection or poisoning detector ships in OSS (the docs' 422 example names a 'prompt_injection' detector, but no code for it exists in the repo).

write.governance.t: Redaction via the opt-in Memory Defense; retain_mission narrows what is extracted; tag-scoped visibility; audit log (off by default); document, memory and bank deletes. No consent model and no TTL on memories: the retention sweep only purges operations, audit and LLM-trace rows.

segment.unit.t: A chunk of at most 3,000 characters (DEFAULT_RETAIN_CHUNK_SIZE). Each chunk gets one extraction call; a retain item smaller than the limit is a single chunk.

segment.rule.t: Size-based. JSON conversation arrays are cut at turn boundaries, keeping whole turns; JSONL is cut at lines; plain text uses recursive separators; image-bearing text has its own budget (1,500 chars per image, at most 8 attachments per chunk). No topic or episode boundary detection.

segment.measured.t: No published per-LoCoMo chunk or call counts found. Inferred: a LoCoMo session (~22 turns) is typically 1-2 chunks of 3,000 chars, so about 300-550 chunks for 272 sessions.

extract.calls.t: One structured-output LLM call per chunk (temperature 0.1, up to 64k completion tokens), with an auto-split retry if output overflows. Optional provider Batch API for async retain (off by default). The 'chunks' mode makes no LLM call.

extract.facts.t: Narrative atomic facts with what/when/where/who/why fields, combined into one fact text. The paper's design is to keep context (e.g. a whole decision) in one fact rather than fragments. Modes: concise (default), verbose, verbatim, custom, chunks.

extract.episode.t: No separate episode narrative or session summary record; narrative context is folded into each fact. The source chunk can be returned with include.chunks.

extract.dates.t: The event date of each item is put into the extraction prompt (weekday plus ISO), and the model returns occurred_start/occurred_end ISO timestamps and a 'when' text for events, so relative dates are resolved at write time. A fallback infers a date from the fact text.

extract.neighbours.t: The extractor sees only the chunk, chunk index, event date, context, metadata and mission; no existing memories are shown. Neighbour-aware reconciliation happens later in consolidation, where related observations are recalled for each batch of new facts.

extract.failure.t: Output-overflow auto-split of the chunk, schema 'shape repair' retry, LLM retries with backoff, degenerate facts rejected, a per-document 'no_facts' outcome metric, and async tasks retried up to 3 times. Documents can be reprocessed with no re-upload.

graph.entities.t: Entities are a field of the same extraction call (people, organisations, places, products, concepts), plus optional controlled-vocabulary key:value entity labels that resolve by exact match only.

graph.resolution.t: Rule-based, no LLM: pg_trgm candidate lookup (threshold 0.3, up to 200 candidates), then score = 0.5 x SequenceMatcher name similarity + 0.3 x co-occurrence overlap + 0.2 x temporal proximity (7-day decay); merge at >= 0.6. In-batch trigram merge at 0.5.

graph.edges.t: Four untyped link kinds between facts, not subject-predicate-object triples: entity (shared entity), temporal (within 24 h, weight max(0.3, 1 - gap/24h)), semantic (kNN top 50 at cosine >= 0.7) and caused_by (the LLM emits fact-index causal relations in the extraction call; on by default).

graph.communities.t: No community detection or clustering. Observation scopes and mental models play the grouping role.

time.fields.t: Per fact: event_date (required), occurred_start, occurred_end (event time), mentioned_at (when told), created_at and updated_at. That is event-time vs learned-time, but there are no valid_from/valid_to or invalidation fields on facts. Observations carry history (50 entries by default).

time.update.t: Raw facts are append-only. Contradictions are handled at the observation layer: a consolidation LLM call per batch of up to 8 new facts emits creates/updates/deletes over related observations. The rules are prefer update, cascade a state change to every affected observation, preserve history ('previously X, now Y'), delete only when superseded, and never do arithmetic.

time.dedup.t: No fact-level dedup at write; only chunk-hash delta retain skips unchanged chunks when a document is re-upserted. Observations are deduped: a new or updated observation at cosine >= 0.97 against its top-5 neighbours triggers an LLM merge/keep adjudication (Postgres only), within the same tag scope.

derive.profile.t: No built-in user profile. The equivalent is a mental model: a user-defined standing question (e.g. 'What are this user's preferences?') whose answer reflect writes, stores and refreshes in the background after consolidation; reading it is a DB read with no LLM call.

derive.entity.t: The paper's entity-summary 'observation network' has been removed. Recall still returns an entities map, but with empty observation lists; the code comment says 'summaries now live in mental models'. The term 'observation' now names consolidated beliefs.

derive.background.t: Auto-consolidation after every retain, delete or update (on by default), run by Postgres-queue workers (10 slots, 500 ms poll); a 300 s reconcile loop; mental-model refresh ticks; graph and vector-index maintenance jobs; webhooks on consolidation.completed.

derive.forget.t: No decay or forgetting of memories. Recency is only a ranking boost (linear over 365 days, plus or minus 10%). An observation cap per scope is unlimited by default. The paper's opinion confidence (reinforce +a, weaken -a, contradict -2a) is gone with the opinion network.

index.embed.t: Local BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (384-d) by default; an ONNX multilingual-e5-small option; hosted options (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, Gemini, Cohere, TEI, LiteLLM and others).

index.lexical.t: Default 'native' Postgres tsvector + ts_rank_cd (TF-IDF style, not true BM25). Pluggable vchord_bm25, pg_textsearch, PGroonga or ParadeDB pg_search for real BM25 and CJK tokenisers.

index.vector.t: pgvector HNSW (ef_search sized to the recall budget, capped at 1000); a vector-index health job; Oracle vector on the Oracle backend.

read.rewrite.t: No query rewriting or HyDE on recall. The reflect agent writes its own sub-queries as tool arguments.

read.analysis.t: Non-LLM query analysis: a dateparser-based analyser (with a Chinese period table) extracts a temporal window from the query, relative to query_timestamp. An optional transformer analyser exists. The query is capped at 500 tokens.

read.legs.t: TEMPR: four arms per fact type run in parallel: semantic (cosine >= 0.3), keyword, graph (link expansion from semantic seeds) and temporal (only when a window is found). Arm depth is set by the budget: low 100, mid 300, high 1000 candidates (adaptive mode optional).

read.temporal.t: Window overlap on occurred/mentioned dates. Candidates inside the window are chosen by semantic relevance (min 0.1), not recency, then spread through links. A temporal-proximity boost is applied at rerank. Callers may pass an explicit temporal_window.

read.traversal.t: One-hop link expansion: graph_score = tanh(0.5 x shared entities) + semantic link weight + causal weight (range 0-3), at most 200 targets per entity and a 10 s timeout. Multi-hop depth is not documented beyond 'explores up to recall_budget nodes'.

rank.fusion.t: Reciprocal rank fusion with k = 60, equal weights by default; optional per-arm strategy boosts and a per-source cap; an interleave alternative exists.

rank.rerank.t: Cross-encoder on the top 300 RRF candidates: local ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 by default (Cohere, ZeroEntropy, Jina, TEI and others optional). Then final = sigmoid(CE) x recency(+/-10%) x temporal proximity(+/-10%) x proof count(+/-5%). The docstring mentions MMR diversity (lambda 0.5), but no MMR code was found.

rank.gate.t: Similarity floors only (semantic 0.3, graph seed 0.3, temporal 0.1, optional caller min_scores). No abstain or relevance gate: the token packer always returns at least the top fact if anything matched.

rank.agentic.t: reflect is a tool-calling agent: search_mental_models, read_mental_models, search_observations, recall (TEMPR), expand and done. Up to 10 iterations, a 100k context cap, a 300 s wall timeout and temperature 0.9. It must gather evidence before answering, cites only retrieved IDs, and verifies stale observations against raw facts. Disposition (skepticism/literalism/empathy 1-5), a mission and hard directives shape it (the paper calls this CARA; the name is absent from code).

answer.shape.t: Recall returns a ranked list of facts and observations (text, type, entities, occurred/mentioned dates, document/chunk ids, tags, scores) plus an optional entities map, raw chunks and source facts. prefer_observations drops raw facts already covered by a returned observation. The caller writes the answer prompt; reflect returns text plus based_on citations.

answer.size.t: Recall max_tokens defaults to 4,096 tokens of fact text (metadata not counted) plus 500 for entities; chunks and source facts are off unless asked. Internal recall uses 2,048 + 1,000 chunk tokens. Benchmark runs: about 36k (vendor LoCoMo, from our notes) and 24,683 (OmniMemEval, from our notes).
answer.size.e: api/http.py:456,528; config.py:1937-1939 [read]; benchmark figures from our notes, not re-verified

answer.prompt.t: No answer prompt in recall. Reflect has its own system prompt (disposition, mission, directives). LoCoMo answer and judge prompts live in the external AMB repo (vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark), not in this repo; the in-repo eval judge defaults to gemini-2.5-flash and must differ from the model under test.

eval.best.t: 92.0 on the vendor leaderboard (LoComo10); 89.61 in the paper (Gemini-3 Pro answerer, GPT-OSS-120b judge).

eval.outside.t: The README says Virginia Tech's Sanghani Center and The Washington Post independently reproduced the numbers (VT authors are co-authors of the paper). The OmniMemEval cloud run, 81.99 at 24.7k context, is about 10 points below the vendor figure.
eval.outside.e: README.md 'Memory Performance & Accuracy' [doc]; OmniMemEval figure from our notes

eval.models.t: Paper: answerers GPT-OSS-20b / GPT-OSS-120b / Gemini-3 Pro; judge GPT-OSS-120b at temperature 0. Vendor site per our notes: Gemini 3.1 Pro preview reader with a Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite 'be generous' judge (the site itself does not name models).

eval.rigour.t: Category split is published, but the paper's LoCoMo token budget is an unfilled '<add> tokens' placeholder and the question count is not stated. The leaderboard omits reader, judge and context. A lenient judge and a strong reader inflate the 92. AMB is pinned to 'main', so harness drift is possible (the repo prints the resolved commit).

cost.write.t: Inferred for 272 sessions / 5,882 turns: about 300-550 extraction calls (one per 3,000-char chunk), plus consolidation at one call per 8 new facts (likely several hundred), plus dedup adjudications for near-duplicate observations and any mental-model refreshes. Entity resolution and links make no LLM calls. Prompt caching of the fixed system prefix is on by default.

cost.read.t: recall: 0 LLM calls (one query embedding, SQL arms, local cross-encoder). reflect: 1-10 LLM tool-loop calls plus optional structured-output or length-rewrite calls.

cost.where.t: Embeddings and reranker run locally by default (CPU, GPU or MPS). The LLM is hosted by default (OpenAI) but any of 25+ providers works, including fully local llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio. Vendor guidance: the small gpt-oss-20b is enough for extraction.

trust.provenance.t: Facts carry document_id, chunk_id, context, metadata and source attachments. Observations carry source_memory_ids (GIN-indexed), quotes, a proof_count and history; reflect returns based_on citations restricted to retrieved IDs. There is no trust score or source-class field.

trust.erasure.t: Deleting a document, memory or bank cascades to derived observations, and the surviving source facts are reset for re-consolidation. A per-memory endpoint clears the observations derived from it. The FK cascades from documents to memory_units.

trust.auth.t: Default DefaultTenantExtension: no authentication, single schema. ApiKeyTenantExtension (a shared bearer key) or a custom extension is opt-in; MCP passes the API key through.

trust.sharing.t: Sharing is by bank (several agents can write to one bank), tags and tag-scoped observations, per-scope consolidation strategies (e.g. company-wide scopes with a stricter mission), bank aliases, and export/import/clone. Agents in one bank have no per-agent trust or write isolation.

extras.t: Standing questions whose reflect-written answers are stored and refreshed after consolidation (50-entry history). They are read with no LLM call and the reflect agent checks them first. Knowledge pages expose them as a folder wiki projectable to markdown.
Consolidation runs per tag scope, one LLM call per scope. A per-scope mission and observation cap let one bank keep private detail for a user scope and generalised trends for a company scope.
Bank-level traits (skepticism, literalism, empathy 1-5) and a mission shape reflect; directives are hard tag-scoped rules applied in reflect.
A per-bank natural-language mission is injected into the variable user turn (so the cached system prefix stays bank-agnostic). Modes are concise / verbose / verbatim / custom / chunks (no LLM).

Images and files sit inline with text in retain content; a separate vision model slot is used only for chunks that carry attachments. Facts keep links to the attachment they came from, and observations inherit them.
Re-upserting a document re-extracts only chunks whose hash changed; unchanged chunks keep their facts, entities and links.
Built-in MCP server (multi-bank or single-bank tool sets), a two-line LLM wrapper, and integrations for coding agents and frameworks.
extras.e: api/mcp.py:114-207; README.md 'Adding Hindsight to Your Agent' [read]

extras.t: Five lexical backends, selectable per deployment, including ParadeDB pg_search for true BM25 on Citus and jieba tokenisation.
Callers ask for max_tokens, not top-k. Packing is in rank order and an oversized fact skips only itself. Search depth (budget low/mid/high) is a separate, independent knob.
Per-core in-flight admission limits for recall, reflect and retain; a global LLM concurrency of 32 with per-operation caps so background consolidation cannot starve live reads.

token_economy.t: Small context is achieved mainly by (1) token-denominated recall: rank-ordered packing to max_tokens (default 4,096; doc recommends 2,048 for chatbots), metadata free; (2) consolidation: many raw facts collapse into one evidence-backed observation, with prefer_observations dropping the raw facts an observation already covers; (3) mental models: precomputed answers read with no retrieval or LLM; (4) narrative facts that carry who/when/where/why so fewer facts answer a question; (5) chunks and source facts off by default; (6) recall has no LLM call at all; (7) provider prompt caching of the fixed extraction system prefix. Measured context per LoCoMo question is about 36k on the vendor run and 24,683 on OmniMemEval (both from our notes), far above the 4k default, so the headline scores use a much larger budget than the default.

speed.t: Read-optimised by design: all LLM work happens at write or in the background. Recall runs four SQL arms in parallel per fact type (4 DB connections per recall), with no LLM; vendor latency is 100-600 ms recall (CPU reranker is the bottleneck; length-bucket batching is 36-54% faster; FP16 on MPS 27-36% faster), 800-3,000 ms reflect, and 500-2,000 ms per retain batch. Writes can be async (Postgres queue, SKIP LOCKED workers, auto-split into sub-batches of ~10k tokens processed concurrently), use the provider Batch API, an embedding coalescer, and consolidation of 8 facts per call with configurable parallelism.

keep: Recall has no LLM: four cheap parallel arms (vector, lexical, one-hop link graph, dateparser temporal window) + RRF k=60 + a small local cross-encoder over 300 candidates, then bounded multiplicative boosts (recency, temporal proximity, proof count; at most +27% / -23% combined).
Budget the context in tokens, not top-k, and keep 'search depth' as a separate knob; pack in rank order so one long item cannot evict shorter ones.

Layered read hierarchy for synthesis: mental models (precomputed, no LLM) then observations (consolidated, with proof counts and staleness flags) then raw facts as ground truth, with prefer_observations deduplicating by provenance.

Do contradiction handling in background consolidation over observations (create/update/delete with history, 'never compute numbers', cascade state changes) and keep raw facts append-only, so the write path stays a single extraction call per chunk.
Speaker-based world/experience routing at extraction, driven by caller context, and the event date in every extraction prompt so relative dates resolve at write time.
avoid: Benchmark opacity: the 92 LoCoMo leaderboard names no reader, judge or context; the paper's LoCoMo token budget is a literal '<add> tokens' placeholder; the vendor run reportedly uses a ~36k context and a 'be generous' judge, against a 4k default; an outside harness gets 81.99.

Architecture drift from the paper: the opinion network (with confidence updates) was deleted in 2026-04 and the entity-summary 'observation' network was replaced by mental models, so the four-network claim describes neither the current code nor the old one.
The write firewall is only secrets/PII regex and off by default; no injection or poisoning defence in OSS, no auth by default, and no per-writer trust on shared banks.

No fact-level dedup or invalidation at write and no forgetting: raw facts grow without bound, and correctness of 'current state' depends on the asynchronous consolidation having caught up (reflect must re-verify stale observations).
